tagline: Cross-post updates, route escalations and share digests between Slack and Microsoft Teams
metaTitle: Slack + Microsoft Teams Integration: Cross-Post and Route
metaDescription: Connect Slack and Microsoft Teams with GAIA: cross-post Slack updates to Teams, route escalations, send digests. For live two-way mirroring, use a bridge.
intro:
This integration connects a Slack workspace and a Microsoft Teams tenant so information posted on one side reaches people on the other. The two apps do not exchange messages out of the box, so you need a third tool, and there are two kinds. A bridge (such as Mio, or the self-hosted Matterbridge) mirrors chat in real time in both directions, message by message. An automation tool like GAIA decides what crosses over: it reads new messages in the channels you pick, then posts announcements, escalations and summaries to the other side by rules you write in plain English.

Pick by what you need. If two groups must hold one live conversation across both apps, with every reply and edit mirrored, use a dedicated bridge: GAIA is not a message mirror. If people on each side need the right information without reading the other platform (leadership announcements, incident escalations, a daily digest of a busy channel), GAIA is the lighter option, and it can do more with each message, such as creating a task, filing a ticket or emailing a partner.

How the two directions work. Slack to Teams is event-driven: the trigger fires when a new message lands in a channel you chose, and the workflow posts to the other side shortly after. The reverse direction runs on a schedule you set (every hour, or each morning), because that app does not push new messages to GAIA. On each run GAIA checks the chats you name and posts what matches your rules into the target channels.

An example workflow: "When someone in the leadership group posts in #announcements, post it to the General channel of the Company team with the author's name and a link back to the original. Every weekday at 5pm, summarize #eng-incidents and post the summary to the Ops team."

useCases.title: Share project updates across Slack and Teams
useCases.description: When a cross-functional project has members on both platforms, GAIA watches the project channel and posts decisions, blockers and status changes to the matching channel on the other side. It forwards what your rules select instead of every message, so the receiving side gets the signal, not a copy of the chatter.

useCases.title: Company announcement cross-posting
useCases.description: When leadership posts in an announcements channel, the trigger fires and GAIA posts the same text to the channel you chose on the other platform, with the author and a link back. One post reaches employees on both platforms.

useCases.title: External partner updates
useCases.description: When your company and an agency use different platforms, GAIA can post a summary of the partner's channel to your channel on a schedule, and post your decisions back to the partner's channel when you ask. For one shared live channel between the two companies, a dedicated bridge fits better.

useCases.title: Escalation routing from Teams to Slack
useCases.description: On a schedule you set, GAIA checks the chats you name for messages that look like escalations (a keyword, a severity tag, a named customer) and posts them to the channel where the senior team works. This direction is scheduled, so pick an interval that matches how urgent your escalations are.

useCases.title: Migration-period dual posting
useCases.description: During a move from one platform to the other, GAIA posts announcements and key channel updates to both so people who have not switched yet still see them. Turn the workflow off once everyone has moved.

useCases.title: Daily cross-platform digest
useCases.description: Every morning GAIA summarizes the busiest Slack channels and posts one digest to a Teams channel: decisions made, open questions, links to the threads. Readers stay informed without joining the source workspace.

howItWorks.description: Authorize both from GAIA's integrations page: your Slack workspace, and your Microsoft 365 account for Teams. GAIA can then read new messages in the channels you pick and post to channels and chats on either side.

howItWorks.step: Describe the workflow in plain English
howItWorks.description: Say which channels to watch, what should cross over (every message, only posts from certain people, only messages that mention a customer), where it goes and how it should read. Add a scheduled workflow for anything that should flow in the reverse direction.

howItWorks.step: GAIA runs it in the background
howItWorks.description: Matching messages from the trigger channels are posted to the destination shortly after they arrive. Scheduled checks run at the interval you set. Each run appears in the workflow's history, so you can see what was posted and tighten the rules.

faqs.question: Can GAIA prevent echo loops where a bridged message gets re-posted infinitely?
faqs.answer: Yes. Point each direction at different channels (for example #announcements to the General channel, and an escalations chat to #support-leads) and no message can bounce back. If you route both ways between the same pair, tell the workflow to skip messages GAIA posted itself.

faqs.question: Does GAIA support file and attachment sharing between the two apps?
faqs.answer: GAIA cross-posts text and can include a link back to the original message, where any file stays. It does not upload a copy of the file to the other platform, so people need access to the source app to open it.

faqs.question: Is this suitable as a permanent setup or only during migrations?
faqs.answer: Either. Keep the workflows running for a long-term dual-platform setup, or switch them off when a migration finishes. If you need full two-way mirroring of whole channels for months, a dedicated bridge suits that better.

faqs.question: Does GAIA keep the channels in the two apps in sync in real time?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA is not a real-time mirror. Messages in the event-driven direction reach the destination shortly after they are posted, because the trigger fires on each new message, but replies, edits, reactions and deletions are not mirrored, and the reverse direction runs on a schedule. For a live two-way bridge, use a dedicated tool such as Mio or Matterbridge. If you are still choosing a primary chat platform, see /compare/teams.

faqs.question: What can GAIA include in a cross-post besides plain text?
faqs.answer: It can add the author, channel, time and a link to the original, and it can rewrite the message before posting: a short summary, a translation, or a formatted announcement. @mentions do not carry over, because the two apps keep separate user accounts, so GAIA writes the person's name instead.

faqs.question: Is there a native integration for sharing messages between the two apps?
faqs.answer: Not for messages. The two apps do not sync chat with each other out of the box. A calls app exists that starts video meetings from within chat, but it does not move messages. For messages your options are a dedicated bridge that mirrors channels, or an automation tool or assistant like GAIA that cross-posts, summarizes and routes selected messages.

faqs.question: How do I connect the two apps with GAIA?
faqs.answer: Connect both apps on GAIA's integrations page. Create a workflow with the new-message trigger and pick the channels to watch. Describe what to post and where, for example: "Post every message from #announcements to the Company team's General channel with the author's name." Save it, post a test message in the source channel, then check the workflow's history.

faqs.question: Can GAIA send Microsoft Teams messages to Slack?
faqs.answer: Yes, on a schedule. Microsoft's side does not notify GAIA about new messages, so a scheduled workflow checks the chats you name (every hour, or each morning) and posts what matches your rules to the channels you chose. For urgent items, choose a short interval, or keep urgent alerts in a channel whose trigger fires right away.
